propositions: The outbound differ compares in vendor shape (Jira-nested keys) while the inbound differ compares in canonical shape, violating the §(d) seam principle that core consumes/produces vendor payloads only at port boundaries.

The outbound update path must canonicalize the snapshot via InboundMapper.map_remote_to_local before comparison, then emit vendor payloads exclusively via OutboundMapper.map_fields_to_remote at the emission boundary, mirroring the inbound differ's canonical-comparison pattern.

InboundMapper output must be widened with three canonical alias keys (assignee_identity, remote_parent_id, reporter_identity) using presence-guard semantics: absent vendor key → absent canonical key, never defaulted, preserving baseline arbitration equivalence.

The assignee resolver (including accountId fast-path and unmappable→unassign soft-fail) must be re-homed to OutboundMapper.resolve_assignee as a parameterized method operating only on canonical assignee_identity shape, keeping dispatch_one.py's _assignee_is_account_id sentinel behavior byte-identical.

map_remote_to_local must tolerate partial vendor dicts (_BASELINE_FIELDS subset) by emitting only canonical keys whose source vendor key is present, while full snapshots map byte-identically to today's behavior.

All vendor payload key literals and adapters.jira imports must be removed from outbound_differ.py; the core module must contain no direct Jira snapshot-shape knowledge, verified by AST denylist and runtime injection spy tests proving canonical comparison and emission-boundary mapping.
